Complete a serve to see your measurements and supported coaching cues.
Mobile study feedback · assessed mechanics only
Processed on this phone. No uploads or account required.

1. Place the phone securely on a tripod on your dominant-hand side. The study used a fixed camera about 2 metres above the ground, angled toward the net.

2. Keep your full body, feet and paddle visible throughout setup and follow-through. Use clear, consistent lighting.

3. Stand ready, then serve normally. Motion starts analysis automatically; results appear after the motion settles.

This model supports right-handed serves. Hip movement and paddle angle are image-plane estimates, not a complete form or legality assessment. General-mechanics cues can appear when serve type is uncertain.

Tip: tap the video or use Menu → Fullscreen camera to frame the shot. Results are spoken aloud so you can stay on the court, and every serve is kept under Menu → Session serves.
GPU pose attempt %1$s. Applies now; falls back to CPU automatically if unsupported. Actual backend is logged.

Original five-fold GRU is the default classifier. The mobile development policy can provide guarded general-mechanics cues when subtype confidence is below 60%. These newer cues were not independently rated by Coach C.

Automatic motion capture can miss serves. Consistent two-second delivery is not established. Ball landing is a separate review tool; its Share QR attaches the zone to a serve on a second phone, fully offline.

All normal analysis stays on this phone. Research exports occur only when explicitly requested.
Camera access is needed for live serve analysis. You can still use the research tools.
Move back into view and keep your full body visible.
Side-view study setup uses the back camera. Front camera is available for input selection.

Drive: flatter, driving swing plane with a firmer paddle face through contact.

Lob: higher, lifting swing plane that sends the ball on a higher arc.

Topspin: steeper low-to-high swing plane with the paddle face brushing up the ball.

These are recorded study categories adapted from pickleball coaching literature (Prime Time Pickleball, 2023). They are not independently validated biomechanical classes. If confidence is below 60%, the serve type is reported as uncertain and only supported general-mechanics cues may appear.
Image-plane hip displacement normalized to body height. Used as a weight-shift proxy only. It is not a full-body form assessment.

Image-plane paddle angle compared with the study reference range. Directional labels (too open / too closed) are available only where validated; otherwise the result is reported as within or outside the reference range.
Ball landing is reviewed here on the receiving half-court — it is not part of live serve analysis. Load a video or use the live feed, and the tracker marks the bounce point.

Landing zones: Deep-Left, Deep-Right, Short-Left, Short-Right. Faults: Fault-Long, Fault-Wide, Fault-Short. These are model estimates, not validated line calls — occlusion and small or blurred balls can still cause missed tracks.
